codex.text: The acceptance rule is under-specified and overfit-prone: the regime definition, volatility bucketing, and the magic 10% expectancy bar are all researcher-tuned, yet you propose a single sealed-holdout peek with no power analysis or multiple-comparison control—on typical firehose per-regime sample sizes, a 10% net-expectancy delta will be statistically indistinguishable from noise, and conditioning itself fragments the sample into thin regimes that flatter the result. "Without invalidating calibration" is unmeasurable as written—name the calibration metric, its tolerated degradation, and which drawdown statistic (max DD? time-under-water?) binds—or the clause is gate theater. Missing validation details: fold count, purge/embargo between walk-forward segments, and proof that regime labels persist out-of-sample rather than reshuffling at the boundary. Finally, commit that the holdout is unsealed exactly once and only after every promote.py gate passes; any iterative re-evaluation against it converts your seal into a second training set.

Experiment: register an exit-research challenger (via ExperimentRegistry) that disables early flattening only for fires in validated states and lets positions resolve at their original TP/SL barriers, à la triple-barrier labeling in *Advances in Financial Machine Learning*, consistent with exit-asymmetry doctrine in *Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom*. codex.text: Pre-register a single regime definition: 20-bar ATR/close, bucketed into low/mid/high terciles using trailing 252-bar training data, with fixed session windows and fold-specific cutpoints frozen out-of-sample. Evaluate a costs-netted ablation in five walk-forward folds with a purge and embargo equal to one maximum holding period, requiring labels and volatility buckets to remain frozen throughout each test segment and each regime to contain at least 200 observations. Accept only if the paired block-bootstrap 95% confidence interval shows a positive net-expectancy improvement of at least 10%, the pre-study power analysis provides at least 80% power for that effect, max drawdown worsens by no more than 1 percentage point, time-under-water by no more than 10%, and Brier score worsens by no more than 0.005; apply Holm correction if more than one challenger is tested. Unseal the holdout exactly once, only after every `promote.py` gate passes, and use it solely for the final decision; any failed gate or inadequate power rejects the candidate without further holdout evaluation.
